title: Discrete lattice derived invariants via a sheaf-module Koszul resolution
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $r\geq0$, and let $P$ be an internal $R$-module [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] equipped with pairwise commuting $R$-linear automorphisms $T_1,\ldots,T_r$. Equivalently $P$ has an action of the discrete group $D=\mathbf Z^r$, whose $i$th basis vector acts as $T_i$. Write $R\Gamma_D$ for the ordinary total right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] of invariants on $D$-equivariant internal $R$-modules. Define the cochain complex $K_R(P;T)$ in degrees $0,\ldots,r$ by
$$K_R(P;T)^a=\bigoplus_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\},\ |I|=a}P,\qquad (dx)_J=\sum_{i\in J}(-1)^{\#\{j\in J:j<i\}}(T_i-1)x_{J\setminus\{i\}}.$$
There is a natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_R:K_R(P;T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_D(P)$$
in the ordinary derived category of internal $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its map from $P^D[0]$ is the degree-zero inclusion of invariant elements into $K_R(P;T)^0=P$. For a morphism $\varphi:R\to R'$ of commutative condensed rings, an internal $R'$-module $P'$ with commuting automorphisms $T'_i$, and an $R$-linear equivariant morphism $f:P\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi P'$ to the scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] (same underlying internal module, $R$ acting through $\varphi$), the square with rows $\lambda_R,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\lambda_{R'}$ and columns the termwise map induced by $f$ and the canonical derived coefficient map $R\Gamma_D(P)\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi R\Gamma_D(P')$ commutes. For $r=0$, $\lambda_R$ is the identity $P[0]$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-lattice-injective-koszul-acyclicity], the displayed signed formula is an additive complex-valued functor $F=K_R$ with exact degree functors. Its natural augmentation $e_P:P^D[0]\to F(P)$ is the invariant inclusion, and $e_J$ is a quasi-isomorphism for each equivariantly injective $J$. By step 1 and [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality], the bounded-below equivariant injective resolutions compute $R\Gamma_D$ through its unit-normalized comparisons. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-exact-complex-derived-model] to $(\mathcal E_R,\mathcal M_R,G,F,e)$: its normalized total-complex span gives $\lambda_R:QK_R(P;T)\cong R\Gamma_D(P)$, natural in $P$, and $\lambda_R Q(e_P)=\eta_{P[0]}$, exactly the required normalization.

proof.text: For $\varphi:R\to R'$, let $U$ and $V$ be restriction on equivariant and underlying modules respectively [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Both are exact: they leave underlying abelian sheaves unchanged, and kernels and sheafified cokernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] are unchanged; equivariant exactness is created on those underlying modules by [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-sheaf-resolution]. Here $GU=VG'$ canonically, since fixed submodules are the same. The finite sums, integer signs and operators give $FU=VF'$ canonically and preserve $e$. Nonnegative injective resolutions compute both $R\Gamma_D$ by [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality]. Thus [lem-sfb-finite-model-restriction-comparison] applies: the unit-normalized coefficient map $\alpha:R\Gamma_D(UP')\cong V R\Gamma_D(P')$ satisfies $\alpha\lambda_R=V\lambda_{R'}$ under this termwise identification. Its inverse is the derived-unit comparison on the restricted resolution $UJ^\bullet$, as the cited statement specifies. Composing with the naturality square from step 2 for $f:P\to UP'$ gives precisely the coefficient square in the statement.

proof.text: For $r=0$, $F=G=\mathrm{id}$, $e=1$ and $K_R(P)=P[0]$. The identity case in [lem-sfb-finite-exact-complex-derived-model] makes $\lambda_R$ the identity under the canonical derived identity comparison. The formulas also hold for the zero module or zero ring. In rank one the differential is $T_1-1$, confirming the invariant augmentation convention.
